utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody in and around the courtroom. Mr. Registrar, please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Good afternoon to everyone in and around the courtroom. This is case number IT-04-81-T, the Prosecutor versus Momcilo Perisic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. Could we have appearances for today, starting with the Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. THOMAS
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours, and everybody in and around the courtroom. Carmela Javier and Barney Thomas for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much. And for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon, Your Honours. Mr. Perisic is represented in court today by Novak Lukic, Gregor Guy-Smith and Boris Zorko.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you so much, Mr. Lukic. Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that we should move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're back in open session, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Are there any housekeeping matters that anybody would like to raise in open session? Mr. Thomas?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. One little matter by the Chamber, an oral decision. On the 22nd of November, 2010, the parties filed publicly a joint stipulation whereby the dates of Incidents 1, 2, 3, 4, 5 and 6, as listed in Schedule B of the indictment, accurately reflect the dates on which those incidents occurred, as found in the Galic trial judgement. The Trial Chamber notes that according to Rule 65 ter (H), the record shall -- I beg your pardon, I'll have to say that again. The Trial Chamber notes that according to Rule 65 ter (H), it shall record the points of agreement and disagreement on matters of law and fact. The Trial Chamber, therefore, records the agreement of the parties regarding the stipulation and makes it part of the trial record. Thank you so much. It does seem as though we can only postpone sine die. Okay. The Chamber postponed sine die. Court adjourned.
